euronews.title: Child protection is not 'only one party's responsibility', business group says
euronews.description: Cecilia Bonefeld-Dahl, Director General of DigitalEurope, said protecting children from social media risks is a "joint responsibility of the public and private sectors". The association, which represents companies such as OpenAI and Meta, believes it cannot be "one party's responsibility".

euronews.description: Canadians in Vancouver reacted to Prime Minister Mark Carney’s proposal for closer ties with the European Union, including possible “associate member” status.

euronews.description: Russia’s parliamentary election is under way, with voting beginning in the Far East on Friday, 18 September before spreading across the country for three days. Polls will remain open until Sunday evening, when voters will have chosen all 450 members of the State Duma.

euronews.title: Russia shares AI-generated Putin selfie as use of artificial content spreads among Europe's politicians
euronews.description: The Russian embassy in South Africa recently shared an AI-generated image of BRICS leaders. It's part of a growing trend of public figures and institutions using AI in their communication, which researchers say can undermine public trust.

euronews.title: Officers fire warning shots as thousands of migrants moved to new facility in Ceuta
euronews.description: Migrants are being moved to a fifth temporary reception space set up to deal with the crisis, which began in late July when more than 70,000 people crossed into Ceuta from Morocco.

euronews.title: Anthropic warns AI is getting closer to building its own successor
euronews.description: Anthropic says its Claude chatbot now leads more than a quarter of the company's research and development, as fears grow that AI systems could soon improve themselves faster than humans can keep up.

euronews.description: Britain is apparently ready to confront the uncomfortable truth: they're really not very good at Eurovision anymore. But why?

euronews.title: 'Remarkable': Scientists discover new wild cat species for first time in 100 years
euronews.description: The Leopardus tilcayo is slightly smaller than a domestic cat, measuring around 45 centimetres - and was first mistaken for a pet.

euronews.title: Ed Sheeran backlash continues as radio station bans songs and Instagram fans unfollow
euronews.description: Ed Sheeran’s turbulent week continues. His music has been pulled from a major Irish radio station and his Instagram followers are leaving him. The fallout from his US tour controversy grows, as the singer is due to return to the stage tomorrow – minus his touring musicians and opening acts.

euronews.title: From Madrid to Zagreb, Europe's autonomous vehicles are multiplying
euronews.description: From Tesla's FSD rollout to driverless lorries connecting Lidl's warehouses, a wave of approvals across the EU shows regulators embracing autonomous mobility faster than expected — and the pace shows no sign of slowing.

euronews.title: South Korean president urges Trump dialogue with Pyongyang
euronews.description: Trump announced in August that he intended to meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un later this year as he once again touted the pair's relationship. Pyongyang has offered little response.

euronews.title: Europeans still believe in the European dream. They just don't think it's within reach, study finds
euronews.description: A new ECFR study finds most Europeans still want a stronger, united Europe, but doubt it's achievable: around 68% see decline, not renewal.

euronews.title: Exclusive: Australian government breaks silence on EU 'associate member' pipe dream
euronews.description: Hot on the heels of the European Union inviting Canada to become an associate member, potentially paving the way for other far-flung nations to join in a similar capacity, the Australian government has addressed its own prospects.

euronews.title: 'Best thing Europe can do' is focus on its internal market, World Economic Forum expert says
euronews.description: Andrew Caruana Galizia, Head of Europe and Eurasia at the World Economic Forum, believes there are certain areas where Europe "will never be able to be self-sufficient, like critical raw materials".

euronews.title: Could the EU Kids Act unwittingly widen the transatlantic AI divide?
euronews.description: Europe must prepare for the potential consequences of implementing further digital rules that could make it more difficult for smaller European developers to compete, warns an industry insider.

euronews.title: Portuguese prime minister outlines plan to tackle rising living costs without changing VAT
euronews.description: Luís Montenegro says the current situation could drag on for some time. But, unlike other European countries, he will not lower the consumption tax.

euronews.title: Greece: Police bust gang using AI to clone relatives' voices for cash
euronews.description: According to the police, the organisation’s illegal proceeds from its activities are estimated to exceed 1 million euros.

euronews.title: EU-Canada relationship is 'not hostile to anybody', Harris says
euronews.description: Irish Finance Minister Simon Harris says details of the new associate membership with Canada "are yet to be determined", but believes it is "good news" that the European Union has signalled its intention to have a "much closer relationship" with Ottawa.

rfi.title: French prosecutors investigate sexual harassment involving smart glasses
rfi.description: French prosecutors have opened a criminal investigation into suspected sexual harassment involving smart glasses, after complaints about women being filmed in the street without their knowledge and the footage being posted online.

rfi.title: Nestlé to face retrial over illegal dumping near French bottled water plants
rfi.description: Nestlé Waters is to face a new trial over alleged illegal dumping near its bottled water plants in eastern France, after an appeals court reinstated key scientific evidence excluded from the original proceedings.

rfi.title: A city at the crossroads of history: Unearthing Gaza's ancient heritage
rfi.description: Before Gaza became synonymous with conflict, it was a place where merchants sold wine from local vineyards, pilgrims crossed continents, fishermen set out before dawn, and generations of families lived between sea and desert. RFI explores its deep history.

rfi.title: Canada and EU 'stronger together' says Carney, brushing aside US threats
rfi.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday welcomed a proposal for his country to become the European Union's first "associate member", shrugging off threats from United States President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: From Peru to the Philippines, defending the land comes at a deadly cost
rfi.description: People defending their land, forests and communities continue to face killings, arrests and intimidation around the world – with Latin America by far the most dangerous region, the environmental campaign group Global Witness has found. In the Philippines, one community resisting a mining project has told RFI of arrests, injuries and legal action against residents trying to stop work on their land.

rfi.title: Dry rivers and shrinking glaciers deepen global freshwater decline
rfi.description: Rivers around the world are running unusually dry as freshwater reserves continue to decline, leaving less water stored away to help countries through drought, the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) has warned. Glaciers and groundwater are also shrinking, while in Switzerland the retreat of Alpine ice is already forcing changes to infrastructure that supplies hydroelectric power.

rfi.title: French fishermen renew protest as France boosts aid over soaring fuel prices
rfi.description: French fishermen renewed protests over rising fuel costs on Thursday despite the government increasing subsidies for the sector and extending support for farmers and construction companies. Diesel prices are nearing a record high, fuelling wider concern over the cost of living and calls for protests reminiscent of the Yellow Vest movement, seven months before the presidential election.

rfi.title: Israel, Morocco agree to open embassies, step up cooperation after US talks
rfi.description: Israel and Morocco have agreed to open embassies in their respective countries following a meeting between their top diplomats and the United States ambassador to the United Nations in New York on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Lebanon security talks in Paris focus on replacing UN mission
rfi.description: The leaders of France, Lebanon and Jordan on Thursday met in Paris to discuss international support for the cash-strapped Lebanese army and the creation of a new force to succeed a longstanding UN peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon.

rfi.title: Trump threatens EU with tariffs over 'laughable' Canada association plan
rfi.description: US President Donald Trump threatened on Wednesday to cut trade with the European Union after the bloc proposed to make Canada its first ever associate member.

rfi.title: Depardieu appeals court order sending him to trial on rape charges
rfi.description: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu is due to ask a Paris appeals court on Thursday to overturn an order sending him to trial over allegations that he raped actor Charlotte Arnould in 2018.

rfi.title: Sudan gold mine collapse kills dozens as search for missing continues
rfi.description: At least 60 people have been killed in the collapse of a gold mine in southern Sudan, with many more still missing and feared dead beneath the rubble.

rfi.title: Abuse survivors set out demands before meeting Pope Leo in France
rfi.description: Seven survivors of sexual violence in the Catholic Church who are due to meet Pope Leo XIV during his visit to France later this month have insisted the talks will not weaken their demands, as five publicly identified themselves on Wednesday.

rfi.title: EU chief calls for European Security Council and closer Canada ties
rfi.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday called for a new European Security Council and closer ties with Canada – setting out plans to strengthen the EU's security, back Ukraine through the winter and reduce its reliance on other countries for trade, technology and critical materials.

rfi.title: DRC opposition condemns violence at protests over constitutional changes
rfi.description: Despite being authorised, an opposition protest in Kinshasa was cut short on Tuesday after clashes broke out and police dispersed demonstrators. The march was part of nationwide action against proposed constitutional changes that opponents say could allow President Félix Tshisekedi to seek a third term.

rfi.title: Pride and joy as Kenya chosen to host 2029 World Athletics Championships
rfi.description: Athletics-mad Kenya is rejoicing after Nairobi was selected to host the 2029 world championships, becoming the first African city to ever stage the event.

rfi.title: Turkey arrests dozens in ongoing crackdown on LGBTQI+ groups
rfi.description: A crackdown on LGBTQI+ groups in Turkey escalated on Tuesday as authorities made dozens of new arrests and police detained protesters in Istanbul and Ankara, following days of raids, arrests and online restrictions across the country.

rfi.title: Former justice minister Rachida Dati goes on trial in Paris over corruption
rfi.description: Rachida Dati, a former French culture and justice minister, goes on trial in Paris on Wednesday accused of corruption and influence peddling over €900,000 she received in consultancy fees from a company linked to Renault-Nissan while serving as an MEP.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, présidentielle 2027 : Emmanuel Macron reçoit les chefs de parti à l’Elysée pour évoquer la « dégradation rapide » de la situation géopolitique et les prix des carburants
lemonde.description: La plupart des principaux candidats à l’élection présidentielle seront présents, de Marine Tondelier à Gabriel Attal ou Raphaël Glucksmann et Bruno Retailleau, à l’exception notable de Marine Le Pen et Jean-Luc Mélenchon, représentés par leur bras droit.

lemonde.title: Delphine Ernotte Cunci, présidente de France Télévisions : « Je tire la sonnette d’alarme sur la sauvegarde de notre modèle culturel »
lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », la patronne du groupe audiovisuel public dévoile une baisse de la dotation de l’Etat de 47 millions d’euros en 2027 et assure que le budget de l’entreprise sera amputé de 90 millions en raison du recul de la publicité et de l’absence de nouvelles cessions immobilières. Une menace à ses yeux pour le financement de la création culturelle française.

lemonde.title: L’« IA générale », un horizon fantasmé qui concentre les peurs, malgré une définition nébuleuse
lemonde.description: Utilisé pour qualifier une IA ayant atteint des capacités supérieures à celles des humains, le terme d’« intelligence artificielle générale » revient régulièrement dans les débats autour des dangers liés à ces technologies. Bien que personne ne semble d’accord sur ce que cela recouvre réellement.

lemonde.title: « L’Espagne est parvenue à contrôler le dérapage de ses comptes publics. Pas la France. »
lemonde.description: Alors que les deux pays avaient vu leur ratio d’endettement bondir au-delà des 100 % de leur PIB, en 2020, le voisin pyrénéen a largement amélioré sa situation. Son principal atout : une croissance supérieure à celle de la zone euro, relève Isabelle Chaperon, chroniqueuse au service Economie du « Monde ».

lemonde.title: Guerre au Moyen-Orient : un pétrolier visé dans le détroit d’Ormuz, le trafic maritime en net recul
lemonde.description: Téhéran revendique une frappe délibérée contre un navire battant pavillon togolais, sur fond de chute du trafic maritime régional et de nouveaux raids saoudiens au Yémen.

lemonde.title: Les violences économiques conjugales et l’épineuse question de la prise en charge des femmes victimes par les banques
lemonde.description: Le principe de non-ingérence des conseillers bancaires et le manque de définition juridique laissent encore de nombreuses femmes démunies.

lemonde.title: Mort de Federico Aramburu : une expertise psychiatrique démolit la ligne de défense de Loïk Le Priol sur le syndrome post-traumatique
lemonde.description: Devant la cour d’assises de Paris, jeudi, la psychiatre Isabelle Teillet a estimé que l’ancien commando de marine ne souffrait pas, au moment des faits, d’un trouble de stress post-traumatique susceptible d’avoir altéré son discernement. Il présente, par ailleurs, toujours « une dangerosité criminologique importante ».

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : les élections débutent en Russie, alors que des dizaines de drones ukrainiens ont été abattus cette nuit dans la région de Moscou
lemonde.description: A partir vendredi se tiennent trois jours de scrutin en Russie pour des élections législatives et locales, un scrutin acquis au parti Russie unie de Vladimir Poutine en l’absence de véritable opposition.

lemonde.title: Pourquoi le kérosène des avions n’est-il pas taxé en France ?
lemonde.description: Chaque semaine, l’équipe du podcast Chaleur humaine répond à vos questions sur la transition climatique

lemonde.title: Marine Le Pen en campagne présidentielle au Porge, village sinistré par les incendies où « personne ne croit plus à la politique »
lemonde.description: Deux mois après les feux en Gironde, la candidate du Rassemblement national a voulu mettre en avant son écoute des victimes. Une visite de campagne diversement appréciée des Porgeais.

lemonde.title: Le Danemark inaugure l’un des premiers sites de stockage de CO₂ « à grande échelle » en Europe
lemonde.description: Dans sa première phase, le projet doit permettre de stocker 400 000 tonnes de CO₂ par an. Ensuite, Ineos prévoit d’injecter 4 à 8 millions de tonnes annuelles, d’ici 2030.

lemonde.title: Après l’été le plus chaud jamais connu en France, le gouvernement envisage de réduire de plus de 30 % le budget de l’Ademe
lemonde.description: Selon les informations du « Monde », l’Agence de la transition écologique verrait son budget d’intervention amputé de plus de 300 millions d’euros.

lemonde.title: La vaccination des enfants en recul dans plusieurs pays d’Europe depuis la pandémie de Covid-19, selon une étude
lemonde.description: D’après une enquête publiée par « The Lancet », sur sept vaccins infantiles étudiés de 1980 à 2024, au moins quatre sont en reflux ces dernières années dans 16 pays de l’Union européenne, la pandémie de Covid-19 ayant marqué un tournant.

lemonde.title: Au procès de Rachida Dati pour « corruption », les tentatives de la défense de repousser son interrogatoire
lemonde.description: La maire du 7ᵉ arrondissement et ancienne ministre est jugée depuis mercredi pour avoir perçu 900 000 euros entre 2010 et 2012 de Renault-Nissan, alors dirigé par Carlos Ghosn. Ce dernier, lui aussi renvoyé pour corruption, sera jugé en son absence.

lemonde.title: Les journées européennes du patrimoine ont lieu ce week-end : nos 10 lieux « perchés » à visiter
lemonde.description: La 43ᵉ édition de la manifestation se tient les samedi 19 et dimanche 20 septembre. Le service Culture du « Monde » dresse une liste de recommandations de sites « perchés ».

lemonde.title: En quoi les infographies de W.E.B. Du Bois ont-elles fait avancer la cause des Afro-Américains ?
lemonde.description: La soixantaine de planches infographiques réalisées par William Edward Burghardt Du Bois, fondateur oublié de la sociologie américaine, présentées lors de l’Exposition universelle de 1900, avaient pour but de combattre les stéréotypes sur les Afro-Américains, quelques décennies seulement après l’abolition de l’esclavage aux Etats-Unis.

france24fr.title: France : "La Niaque. Comment devenir plus que soi", un ouvrage de Jacques Attali
france24fr.description: Jacques Attali, ancien conseiller de François Mitterrand, président de l'ONG "Positive Planet" et auteur de nombreux livres était invité sur France 24. Son dernier ouvrage publié par les éditions Flammarion s’intitule : "La Niaque. Comment devenir plus que soi".

france24fr.title: Israël : Netanyahu amplifie ses menaces contre les réalisateurs du documentaire "Naza"
france24fr.description: Une semaine après avoir reçu le prix spécial du jury à la Mostra de Venise, le 13 septembre, les réalisateurs du documentaire "Naza" sont très critiqués en Israël. Benjamin Netanyahu lui-même exige la révocation de leur citoyenneté.

france24fr.title: France : la colère des pêcheurs retombe, les blocages levés
france24fr.description: La ministre déléguée à la Mer et à la Pêche, Catherine Chabaud, a annoncé vendredi 18 septembre, au lendemain d'une réunion de six heures à Paris avec les représentants des pêcheurs de Méditerranée, qu'elle viendrait lundi 21 à leur rencontre au Grau-du-Roi (Gard) et à Sète (Hérault).

france24fr.title: Budget 2027 en France : 54 milliards d'économie prévus, un objectif "ambitieux mais réalisable"
france24fr.description: En France, les discussions autour du budget 2027 prennent place. Le gouvernement annonce "54 milliards d'efforts sur les dépenses qui amènent, du coup, le déficit public à 5 % l'année prochaine", a-t-il ajouté, après des annonces en ce sens du Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu. Cet objectif de déficit "est ambitieux, mais évidemment, il est réalisable. Il va falloir qu'on fasse tous des efforts", a estimé Roland Lescure, ministre de l'Économie.

france24fr.title: Ebola progresse au Nord-Kivu, ambassades Israël-Maroc, des Mondiaux au Kenya : l'hebdo Afrique
Yémen : les affrontements entre les Houthis et le gouvernement obligent les habitants à fuir
france24fr.description: Les affrontements entre les forces gouvernementales yéménites et les Houthis au Yémen ont fait 63 morts dans les deux camps ces dernières 24 heures, des combats qui poussent des milliers de personnes à fuir.

france24fr.title: Élections législatives en Russie : un scrutin observé par le Kremlin
france24fr.description: En Russie, le vote pour renouveler les 450 sièges de la Douma, la chambre basse du Parlement russe, est prévu pour durer jusqu'à dimanche 20 septembre à 18 h 00 GMT. Les premiers résultats doivent tomber dans la foulée. Les précisions de Gauthier Rybinski, chroniqueur international à France 24.

france24fr.title: ICE au Texas : vivre dans la peur
france24fr.description: Depuis le retour de Donald Trump, plus de 400 000 personnes ont été placées en détention par ICE, la police fédérale de l'immigration et près de 60 000 migrants y sont enfermés. Mais que deviennent les personnes arrêtées ? Dans quelles conditions vivent-elles ? Et pourquoi des enfants sont-ils eux aussi détenus ? Enquête de Pierrick Leurent et Valérie Defert au Texas.

france24fr.title: Après le transfert de leurs actifs à une société russe, Auchan et Nestlé cherchent la parade
france24fr.description: Alors que Vladimir Poutine a ordonné le placement sous "administration temporaire" des actifs russes de Nestlé et de trois entreprises françaises, selon un décret publié jeudi, le géant de l'agroalimentaire suisse dit prendre acte et évaluer ses options, tandis que le distributeur français Auchan affirme avoir demandé des "clarifications".

france24fr.title: Feu vert de l'administration Trump à la vente de 48 F-35 à l'Arabie saoudite
france24fr.description: L'administration Trump a approuvé jeudi la vente de 48 avions de combat furtifs F-35 à l'Arabie saoudite, pour un montant de 24,3 milliards de dollars. Le projet doit encore être examiné par le Congrès, où des élus s'inquiètent notamment que la technologie de l'appareil ne fuite vers la Chine.

france24fr.title: Russie : coup d'envoi des législatives sur fond de guerre avec l'Ukraine
france24fr.description: Les bureaux de vote ont ouvert vendredi en Russie pour trois jours de législatives, les premières depuis le début de la guerre à grande échelle en Ukraine en 2022. En l'absence de véritable opposition, le parti de Vladimir Poutine devrait remporter ce scrutin, également organisé dans les territoires ukrainiens occupés et annexés par Moscou.

france24fr.title: Le Congrès américain adopte un nouveau paquet de sanctions contre la Russie
france24fr.description: Les députés américains ont approuvé de nouvelles sanctions contre la Russie et ses alliés pour leur rôle dans la guerre contre l'Ukraine, un texte soutenu par Donald Trump dont Kiev a salué l'adoption jeudi. Il donne surtout au président américain le pouvoir d'imposer des droits de douane pouvant atteindre jusqu'à 100 % sur les cinq principaux pays importateurs de gaz et de pétrole russes, dont la Chine et l'Inde.

france24fr.title: Équipe de France : Zidane va-t-il tout changer ? Sa première liste dévoilée aujourd'hui
france24fr.description: Zinedine Zidane entre dans le vif du sujet en divulguant vendredi sa première liste de joueurs depuis sa nomination à la tête de l'équipe de France fin juillet. L'icône du football tricolore va-t-il miser sur la continuité avec son prédécesseur Didier Deschamps ou imprimer sa marque avec l'arrivée de plusieurs nouveaux visages ? Réponse vendredi à 18 h.

france24fr.title: Coup d'envoi des législatives en Russie sur fond de guerre avec l'Ukraine
france24fr.description: Les bureaux de vote ont ouvert vendredi en Russie pour trois jours de législatives, les premières depuis le début de la guerre à grande échelle en Ukraine en 2022. En l'absence de véritable opposition, le parti de Vladimir Poutine devrait remporter ce scrutin, également organisé dans les territoires ukrainiens occupés et annexés par Moscou.

france24fr.title: Le Venezuela débloque l'accès en ligne à plusieurs médias censurés depuis des années
france24fr.description: La levée partielle de la censure numérique a commencé jeudi au Venezuela, alors que pouvoir et opposition ont entamé un deuxième cycle de négociations. Au moins 188 sites, dont 79 médias, restent toutefois bloqués selon une ONG de défense des droits numériques, et un ancien maire d'opposition a été arrêté.

france24fr.title: Au Nigeria, 37 mineurs en situation illégale retrouvés morts en détention
france24fr.description: Le gouverneur de l'État du Niger, au Nigeria, a annoncé jeudi l'ouverture d'une enquête après la mort de 37 mineurs en situation illégale en détention. Les décès sont imputés à la surpopulation carcérale et à une ventilation insuffisante dans un centre de détention de la Défense civile. Le drame a déclenché des manifestations et le report du début de la campagne électorale.

france24fr.title: Un policier d'ultradroite écroué à Paris pour préparation d'acte terroriste
france24fr.description: Un policier de 35 ans adhérant à une "idéologie d'ultradroite radicale violente" a été écroué le 27 août pour préparation d'un acte terroriste et fabrication d'armes imprimées en 3D. Il est soupçonné d'avoir visé des intérêts de l'État dans un contexte de vigilance accrue des autorités françaises face à la menace d'ultradroite.

france24fr.title: En direct : des centaines de drones visent Moscou au premier jour des législatives russes
france24fr.description: La défense anti-aérienne russe a détecté 350 drones ukrainiens volant vers Moscou dans la nuit vendredi, premier jour des élections législatives et locales en Russie, a indiqué le maire de la ville, Sergueï Sobianine. La plupart des engins ont été détruits sur le trajet, dont 64 alors qu'ils étaient à l'approche de la capitale. Suivez notre direct.

zeit.title: Ölindustrie: Wer an der Ölkrise verdient – und wer verliert
zeit.description: Ölpreise steigen dramatisch, Tanker fahren Umwege, Sanktionen greifen nicht mehr: Die Eskalation am Golf stellt den Ölmarkt auf den Kopf – mit überraschenden Gewinnern.

zeit.title: Teures Autofahren: Dieselpreis klettert weiter - Super E10 minimal günstiger
Explosionen: Mindestens 14 Tote bei Anschlag mit Autobombe in Pakistan
Südchinesisches Meer: Philippinen werfen China gefährliches Ramm-Manöver vor
Wahlen in Berlin und Schwerin: «Vor Kraft kaum laufen»? - AfD hofft auf nächsten Schub
Schwerer Unfall endet tödlich: Ein Monat nach Unfall mit Traktor: Frau erliegt Verletzungen
Verkehrskontrolle: Lastwagen-Fahrer fährt bis zu 30 Stunden ohne Pause
Gesundheit: Barmer: Zahnvorsorge kommt bei Pflegebedürftigen oft zu kurz
Drohnenteile bei Wunstorf: Bundesanwaltschaft prüft nach Drohnenfund Verbindung zu Leipzig
zeit.description: Nach dem Fund von Drohnenteilen nahe einem Militärflughafen in Niedersachsen ermitteln die Behörden. Die Teile haben eine ähnliche Bauweise wie die Leipziger Drohne.

zeit.title: Kindheit: Lasst sie doch einfach ein bisschen mehr in Ruhe
zeit.description: Wir schützen Kinder so umfassend wie nie – und erleben gleichzeitig eine Generation, die sich extrem erschöpft und belastetet fühlt. Ein Widerspruch? Nur scheinbar.

zeit.title: AfD-Anhänger: Warum Bernd und René mir sympathisch waren
zeit.description: Ich habe unter AfD-Anhängern Nazis getroffen und Arschlöcher. Aber auch Bernd und René. Wer es mit der Demokratie ernst meint, sollte sich um sie bemühen.

zeit.title: Landtagswahl in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: Livechat: Kann Manuela Schwesig die AfD stoppen?
zeit.description: Schwesigs SPD hat gegen die AfD enorm aufgeholt. Wie gut stehen ihre Chancen – und welche Probleme drohen? Diskutieren Sie jetzt live mit ZEIT-Experte Martin Nejezchleba.

zeit.title: Wahlumfragen zu Landtagswahlen 2026: Das sagen die Umfragen für Berlin und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern
zeit.description: Die SPD holt in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern die AfD ein, in Berlin ringen derzeit vier Parteien um die Spitze. Unsere Übersicht aller Umfragen für die Landtagswahlen 2026

zeit.title: Hans-Joachim Watzke: DFB-Vizepräsident fordert Ablösung von Infantino »ohne Wenn und Aber«
zeit.description: DFB-Vizepräsident fordert Ablösung von Infantino »ohne Wenn und Aber«.

spiegel.title: Perth in Australien: Hai tötet Schwimmer vor westaustralischer Küste
spiegel.description: In Australien ist ein Mann bei einem Haiangriff ums Leben gekommen. Erst vor wenigen Tagen hatte es ebenfalls an der Westküste des Landes eine Attacke mit einem Schwerverletzten gegeben.

spiegel.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: Wie real ist die Gefahr durch bösartige Superintelligenz?
spiegel.description: Jetzt warnen selbst Techbosse vor der Auslöschung der Menschheit durch wildgewordene KIs. Doch was ist dran an der Gefahr? Die wichtigsten Fakten und Einordnungen im Videoexplainer.

spiegel.title: Bundestrainer Jürgen Klopp: Grenzen setzen, Menschen überzeugen – So funktionieren Klopps Kommunikationstricks
spiegel.description: »Fahne zurückholen«, »einer von 83 Millionen«: Jürgen Klopp kann Spieler und Publikum in den Bann ziehen. Aber wie gelingt das dem Bundestrainer? Hier erklärt Kommunikationsexperte Dirk Metz die Methoden – und welches Kalkül dahintersteckt.

spiegel.title: Türkei: Warum sitzt Ferdi Soylu aus Ulm seit einem Monat in Ankara in Haft?
spiegel.description: Der Ulmer Ferdi Soylu wird im Urlaub in der Türkei festgenommen. Ihm wird die Mitgliedschaft in einem Verein mit angeblicher Nähe zur Gülen-Bewegung vorgeworfen. Seine Familie fühlt sich vom Auswärtigen Amt alleingelassen.

spiegel.title: Konjunkturprognose: Industrie rechnet mit stärkerem Wachstum
spiegel.description: Der Bundesverband der Deutschen Industrie blickt deutlich optimistischer auf die Konjunktur als bisher. Noch dieses Jahr traut er der deutschen Wirtschaft ein Wachstum von einem Prozent zu.

spiegel.title: Dreh als Comic-Bösewicht – Lars Eidinger hat sich in Hollywood verliebt ❤️
spiegel.description: Lars Eidinger fand die Dreharbeiten zum neuen »Superman«-Film offenbar so toll, dass er gar nicht nach Deutschland zurückwollte. Auch wenn sie in Hollywood mit Pepsi kochen.

spiegel.title: Kampfflugzeug F-35: Was Deutschlands erster Tarnkappenjet kann
spiegel.description: In Texas übergibt die Rüstungsschmiede Lockheed Martin Verteidigungsminister Pistorius die erste F-35 für die Luftwaffe. Der Flieger soll Deutschlands nukleare Teilhabe sichern – und Russland abschrecken.

spiegel.title: Max Riese: Ultra-Radsportler stirbt bei Unfall in Salzburg
spiegel.description: Der erfolgreiche Extrem-Radsportler Max Riese ist tot. Der Sieger des »Hellenic Mountain Race« kam bei einem Straßenunfall ums Leben. Die Polizei geht davon aus, dass er mit einem Hirsch kollidierte.

spiegel.title: »Tatort« aus Köln: »Die letzten Menschen von Köln« im Schnellcheck
spiegel.description: Die Russen haben NRW mit Atomraketen angegriffen, in Köln flüchten die Menschen in Bunker. So proben es jedenfalls ein paar Prepper in diesem »Tatort«, der mit Limoncello und Vicky Leandros Bombenstimmung verbreiten soll.

spiegel.title: Spritpreis: Drei Euro für Benzin? Lasst endlich die Konzerne zahlen
spiegel.description: Der Frust über hohe Benzinpreise steigt mit jedem Cent. Und das vor den Landtagswahlen. Die Regierung sollte endlich die Milliardengewinne der Konzerne besteuern. Drei Zahlen sprechen klar dafür.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz fährt manchmal S-Bahn, sagt Friedrich Merz
spiegel.description: Der Bundeskanzler ein abgehobener Privatjetpilot? Ach, i wo! Friedrich Merz nimmt in Berlin auch gern mal die S-Bahn. Wohin führt seine persönliche Mobilitätswende?

spiegel.title: Microsoft-Manager Brent Hecht: KI womöglich »größter Diebstahl [...] in der Geschichte der Menschheit«
spiegel.description: Die »New York Times« wirft KI-Anbietern vor Gericht vor, ihre Systeme illegal mit Millionen von Artikeln trainiert zu haben. Bisher bestritten sie das, doch nun tauchen brisante Aussagen eines Microsoft-Managers auf.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: Erzeugerpreise in Deutschland steigen stärker als erwartet
spiegel.description: Erzeugerpreise gelten als Barometer für die Inflation und können damit Hinweise geben auf die wirtschaftliche Stabilität des Landes. Neueste Daten zeigen: Sie steigen hierzulande weiter – und schneller als gedacht.

spiegel.title: Schweiz: Großbank UBS droht mit Wegzug
spiegel.description: In der Schweiz wird über schärfere Kapitalvorschriften für Banken gestritten. Die traditionsreiche UBS fürchtet einschneidende Maßnahmen und übt deshalb vor entsprechenden Abstimmungen öffentlich Druck aus.

spiegel.title: Sharon Stone über »Basic Instinct«: »Die Leute haben Angst vor mir«
spiegel.description: Sie wurde als Männermörderin in »Basic Instinct« berühmt, das hat offenbar bis heute Auswirkungen: Sharon Stone erzählt von dem Effekt, den sie auf andere hat – und wie wenig die Rolle mit ihr selbst zu tun hat.

spiegel.title: AfD-Erfolg: Warum es nicht gut ist, rein taktisch zu wählen – Meinung
spiegel.description: Liberale sollen sich in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern dazu durchringen, links zu wählen? Linke sollen den Grünen ihre Stimme geben? Hauptsache, die AfD gewinnt nicht? Das kann keine Lösung sein.

spiegel.title: Ex-OpenAI-Forscher fordert Stopp: »Wir müssen die KI-Entwicklung im Wesentlichen abschalten«
spiegel.description: Der frühere OpenAI-Mitarbeiter Daniel Kokotajlo fordert einen sofortigen Entwicklungsstopp der Technologie. Er warnt vor einer Super-KI, die nicht mehr zu kontrollieren ist – und der Gefahr eines dritten Weltkriegs.

spiegel.title: Los Angeles: Crash im Gegenverkehr – Autofahrerin droht lebenslange Haft
spiegel.description: Sie fuhr mutmaßlich zu schnell und unter Drogeneinfluss: Eine SUV-Fahrerin soll in Los Angeles eine tödliche Kollision verursacht haben. Im Anschluss stürzte die Crew eines TV-Hubschraubers ab, die über den Unfall berichtete.

nzz.title: Mindestens sechs Tote bei einem Schusswaffenangriff an Schule auf den Philippinen
nzz.description: Auch der Angreifer ist offenbar unter den Toten. Laut den Behörden sind mindestens siebzehn weitere Schüler zum Teil schwer verletzt worden.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Tote nach russischen Angriffen im Gebiet Schitomir
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Video zeigt Angriffe auf Huthi-Stellungen +++ USA wollen Saudiarabien 48 moderne F-35-Kampfjets verkaufen
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Mario Fehr will eine fünfte Amtszeit – der parteilose Zürcher Sicherheitsdirektor tritt im April erneut an. Er sei immer noch erstaunlich fit
nzz.description: Wenn er die nächste Legislatur durchzieht, kommt er auf zwei Jahrzehnte im Amt und wäre am Ende 72-jährig. Das macht ihm keine Sorgen.

nzz.title: Nestlé-Geschäft in Russland unter Zwangsverwaltung – der Schritt könnte die Versorgungssicherheit gefährden
nzz.description: Nach dem Beginn des Ukraine-Kriegs ist Nestlé in Russland geblieben. Im Vergleich zu anderen Fällen ist der Angriff auf den Konzern deshalb eher ungewöhnlich.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Bank of Japan erhöht Leitzins auf höchsten Stand seit 31 Jahren
Katy Perry: wie ein sechzehn Jahre alter Song zum Sommerhit wurde
nzz.description: Ein Lied aus dem Jahr 2010 wird zum «Global Song of the Summer» – es handelt von der Sehnsucht nach dem Vergangenen. Die Gen Z entdeckt ihre melancholische Seite.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Den globalen Süden gibt es nicht – der Mythos hilft Diktatoren, Linkspopulisten und ehrgeizigen Politikern
nzz.description: Am Brics-Gipfel in Delhi beschworen Xi Jinping, Wladimir Putin und Narendra Modi ihre Einigkeit. Ein Blick auf die Realpolitik zeigt: Die Länder Südamerikas, Afrikas und Asiens sind viel zu verschieden, als dass sie einen Block bilden könnten. Hinter der Fassade schwelen die Konflikte.

nzz.title: Zuerst der F-35 und jetzt Röstis Verkehrskonzept: Warum die Finanzkontrolle meist recht hat und trotzdem halb Bern schon verärgert hat
nzz.description: Beim F-35-Kampfjet wurden ihre Warnungen ignoriert, nun zerlegt sie Albert Röstis Verkehrskonzept. Die Eidgenössische Finanzkontrolle ist so präsent wie selten – doch ihre Rolle ist umstritten. Das hat auch mit ihrem ehemaligen Chef Michel Huissoud zu tun.

nzz.title: Kampf um Strom und Wasser: Ein Schweizer Weltmarktführer zeigt das grosse Paradox beim Siegeszug von KI
nzz.description: Künstliche Intelligenz wird immer effizienter und braucht doch immer mehr Ressourcen. Es ist einer der ältesten Widersprüche des Fortschritts – bis zurück zur Dampfmaschine.

nzz.title: Plug-in-Hybride im Kleinwagensegment: BYD drückt mit dem Dolphin G auch hier die Preise
nzz.description: Der neue kleine BYD setzt mit Kampfpreisen, üppiger Reichweite und viel Technik die etablierten Hersteller unter Druck – und zeigt, wie weit die Chinesen bei der Produktreife sind.

nzz.title: Russlands Wahlergebnis steht praktisch fest. Interessant ist, was sich trotzdem verändert hat
nzz.description: Russland wählt am Wochenende ein neues Parlament. Die Opposition ist weitgehend ausgeschlossen. Doch seit der letzten Duma-Wahl ist der Krieg im Alltag deutlich spürbarer geworden. Das verunsichert die Bevölkerung.

nzz.title: Dem Basler Messebetreiber MCH macht die Krise in Dubai zu schaffen
nzz.description: Wegen des Iran-Kriegs wurden im ersten Halbjahr zahlreiche Kongresse und Kundenanlässe in der Golfregion abgesagt. MCH setzt trotzdem auf eine Erholung. Die Kunstmesse Art Basel soll 2027 weiterhin auch in Katar stattfinden.

nzz.title: Die Milliardärin Kim Kardashian erhält einen Dollar Schadenersatz – und freut sich
nzz.description: Vor zehn Jahren wurde Kim Kardashian ausgeraubt. Noch immer erfährt sie nicht nur Empathie, sondern auch Häme.

nzz.title: «Rübermachen» und Teil eines anderen Bundeslandes sein? Eine Thüringer Gemeinde probt den Aufstand
nzz.description: Weil sich Gerstungen von der Landesregierung in Erfurt verlassen fühlt, lanciert der Bürgermeister einen gewagten Vorstoss: Könnten die Thüringer nicht zu Hessen werden? Der Entscheid des Gemeinderats ist da eindeutig.

nzz.title: «Schulden verbrennen», «Rente mit 62»: Frankreichs Populisten operieren trotz Finanznot mit schönen Wahlversprechen
nzz.description: Mehr als 3500 Milliarden Euro Schulden und immer höhere Zinskosten setzen Frankreich unter Druck. Premierminister Sébastien Lecornu verschärft deshalb seinen Sparkurs. Doch Linke und Rechte versprechen den Wählern das Blaue vom Himmel.

observador.title: Para onde vai a geopolítica no Iémen e na Europa?
observador.description: Major-general Arnaut Moreira considera que o contexto internacional mudou, evidencia o conflito no Iémen, os riscos de segurança na Europa e ainda a evolução da Coroa britânica.

observador.title: Streisand critica Trump por ameaçar demolir Kennedy Center
observador.description: Declarações da cantora surgem após juiz determinar que Trump deve avisar com antecedência a intenção de demolição. Streisand recorda homenagem a John Kennedy e critica "contenda pelo protagonismo".

observador.title: Qual é o custo da incerteza para as PMEs?
observador.description: No novo episódio, Alexandre Martins e Joana Carvalho explicam por que gerir riscos ESG é vital para a sobrevivência e financiamento das PME.

observador.title: Indonésia reforça defesa com porta-aviões italiano
observador.description: O navio, fora de serviço desde 2024, chega ao país numa iniciativa com o governo italiano para reforçar a cooperação entre as duas nações. Deverá ser utilizado para combate a catástrofes naturais.

observador.title: Azambuja. Aluno que esfaqueou colegas já não está na escola
observador.description: Dois anos depois do ataque na Escola Básica 1, 2 e 3 da Azambuja, o jovem que esfaqueou seis colegas já não frequenta a escola. Direção reforçou segurança e vítimas ainda estão a ser seguidas.

observador.title: O fantasma Passos, teimosia na CPI e o custo para o Governo
observador.description: O plano de Passos para o País que desafia Montenegro, a guerra Ventura e Aguiar-Branco sobre CPI a Neves e os efeitos do custo de vida na vida do Governo foram os temas da Vichyssoise

observador.title: 10h. Começa a esta hora o debate de urgência pedido pelo PS
observador.description: Os socialistas criticam o Governo por não estar a fazer o suficiente para colmatar a subida geral dos preços. Ainda, o CHEGA acusa o Governo de apresentar medidas de propaganda.

observador.title: Custo de vida: Governo devia (ou podia) ir mais longe?
observador.description: Rui Afonso (CH) critica "medidas de propaganda". António Mendonça Mendes (PS) fala em "insensibilidade" do Governo. Paulo Núncio (CDS) rejeita regresso à bancarrota. As medidas do Governo em debate.

observador.title: Qual é o custo da incerteza para as PMEs?
observador.description: No novo episódio, Alexandre Martins e Joana Carvalho explicam por que gerir riscos ESG é vital para a sobrevivência e financiamento das PME.

observador.title: Encontros da Imagem em Braga, Guimarães, Porto e Avintes
observador.description: Cooper & Gorfer, César Dezfuli, Ciril Jazbec, Tânia Dinis e Eurico Lino do Vale são alguns dos nomes que compõem o programa daquele que é o mais antigo festival de fotografia de Portugal.

observador.title: China defende "estabilidade estratégica" com EUA
observador.description: Contacto acontece na reta final dos preparativos para um eventual encontro entre Xi e Trump em Washington, embora a China ainda não tenha confirmado oficialmente a visita do líder chinês aos EUA.

observador.title: Poderá o Governo proteger o país sem risco de Troika?
observador.description: Os apoios do Governo focam no IRS e nos idosos enquanto os transportes exigem eficiência. E ainda, o jogo soma 3.000€ apostados por adulto com risco de vício.

observador.title: Malásia. Rei autoriza prisão domiciliária de ex-governante
observador.description: Decisão do Rei constitui uma utilização sem precedentes da prisão domiciliária como forma de clemência real no país e poderá reabrir o debate sobre os poderes da monarquia e a aplicação da lei.

observador.title: Austrália passará a prender turistas com visto expirado
observador.description: Ministro do Interior diz querer demonstrar que "o Governo controla a imigração". Indústria do turismo e organizações de direitos humanos criticam medidas, alegando impactos sociais e económicos.

observador.title: Jornadas Europeias do Património com centenas de atividades
observador.description: Portugal recebe 400 atividades durante as Jornadas Europeias do Património. O mote desta edição é "Reviver, resistir, reinventar" de forma a refletir sobre as mudanças e a digitalização da sociedade.

phys-org.title: Early heat waves hit wheat yields hardest but boost resilience to subsequent heat waves
phys-org.description: New research published in the Journal of Experimental Botany reveals that wheat crops are more sensitive to grain yield losses from heat waves that occur before reaching their flowering stage than those occurring later. However, exposure to heat waves early in the growing season may reduce yield losses during additional heat waves through a protective "priming" effect.

phys-org.title: Could expanding the U.S. nuclear arsenal make Americans less safe?
phys-org.description: A new report from the Brookings Institution presents evidence that increasing the size of the U.S. nuclear arsenal could make nuclear crises more likely. This raises an important challenge to arguments that the U.S. must consider increasing its stockpile in response to China's growing nuclear capabilities.

phys-org.title: Baby orangutans in India expose 'frightening' scale of trafficking

phys-org.title: Bolivia's tilcayo tiger cat becomes first new wildcat species in 100 years

phys-org.title: Grass and clover can provide more than animal feed
phys-org.description: Growing leys—grass and clover—is nothing new in Swedish agriculture. But in the arable farming regions dominated by cereal production, leys are less common. One reason is that there needs to be a market for what is harvested.

phys-org.title: In hottest summer on record, 2 in 3 Americans say climate change is increasing heat-related illnesses
phys-org.description: Nearly two-thirds of the American public say climate change is increasing the risk of respiratory diseases and heat- and insect-related illnesses, according to a new survey from the Annenberg Public Policy Center (APPC) of the University of Pennsylvania.

phys-org.title: When prepping for disaster, don't forget to pack your teddy bear

phys-org.title: Robots grow and package lettuce year-round in Norway's fully automated farm
phys-org.description: Norway's first fully automated facility for vegetable production was put into operation last fall. This spring, the first products hit store shelves.

phys-org.title: Museums on prescription: How cultural activities are becoming crucial to the public health debate
phys-org.description: On June 18, 2026, on the sidelines of the European Council in Brussels, the European Parliament, the European Commission and the Council of the European Union signed a joint declaration making culture a strategic priority for the first time.

phys-org.title: Toxic algae can pose a hidden danger to dogs swimming in freshwater
phys-org.description: Diving into cool water can be a quick way to escape the summer heat, but during certain times of year, freshwater can pose hidden dangers to people and pets.

phys-org.title: From toothbrushes to aerospace: Graphene research advances fibers that conduct heat efficiently
phys-org.description: KAIST's discovery of graphene oxide liquid crystals in 2011 laid the foundation for 15 years of research worldwide, leading to technologies for producing graphene fibers with high strength and thermal conductivity. The fundamental materials research that helped bring antibacterial toothbrushes and functional sportswear to market is now advancing into materials for thermal management.

phys-org.title: Europe's earliest glacier loss day in years signals a reckoning for the Alps
phys-org.description: On June 29, 2026, the snow accumulated by Switzerland's glaciers over the course of the previous winter had melted. Known as Glacier Loss Day, this date marks the point at which further melting begins to erode the glaciers' mass until snow accumulation resumes in the fall. Matthias Huss, the network head of Glacier Monitoring in Switzerland (GLAMOS), told Agence France-Presse (AFP) that this year's Glacier Loss Day was "three months too early, compared to a healthy state."

phys-org.title: Fossil plankton shells reveal reduced nitrogen fixation in warmer oceans 3 million years ago
phys-org.description: Nitrogen is a key nutrient because it fuels the growth of plankton, which forms the basis of the marine food web. Two opposing processes determine the global nitrogen cycle: nitrogen fixation and denitrification.

phys-org.title: Circular economy pilot projects show hotels can reduce waste and costs
phys-org.description: The new EU Packaging Regulation (PPWR) has been in effect since Aug. 12, 2026. Under this regulation, beginning in January 2030, the food service industry may no longer buy food or toiletries packaged in single-use plastic—for example, ketchup packets or individually wrapped bars of soap. This is increasing pressure on hotels, restaurants and catering businesses to act.

phys-org.title: A finely tuned mess—how disorder can make networks more stable
phys-org.description: Perfection is overrated—at least when it comes to complex systems like the power grid, food webs and advanced materials. For decades, scientists generally assumed that networks function most reliably when their individual components are as similar as possible. But real-world networks are rarely uniform.

phys-org.title: Developing new asymmetric catalytic reactions for the synthesis of complex molecules
phys-org.description: Do Hyun Ryu's research team in the Department of Chemistry at Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) has developed two new asymmetric catalytic methods for the precise synthesis of complex molecules using chiral organic catalysts.

phys-org.title: Report on global water resources: Worldwide continents are drying up
phys-org.description: The global water cycle is becoming increasingly unbalanced. Extreme droughts and floods are the result. This is shown in this year's report by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) on the state of global water resources, "State of Global Water Resources 2025," which was published today.

phys-org.title: Ubiquitin marks abnormal glycogen for destruction to protect the brain, study finds
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Cambridge and the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology have discovered a previously unknown cellular defense system that protects the brain from abnormal glycogen accumulation, which is linked to severe neurological disorders.

undark.title: Review: A Vision of a Future Where Machines Fight Wars
undark.description: In “Lethal Autonomy,” Frank Kendall, a former top defense department official, envisions a military future where vehicles and weapons operate largely on their own — including making some decisions to strike people or infrastructure. And in his view, conflict is coming to space, making it all more urgent.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Iran Sanctions Have a China Problem
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump is trying to pressure the Iranian regime by isolating it from the dollar-based financial system. But because Iran’s oil trade largely moves through Chinese banks and renminbi-based networks, those sanctions increasingly depend on financial institutions beyond American control.

proj-syn.title: When AI Stops Asking Permission
proj-syn.description: The most useful lesson from this summer’s breach of Hugging Face by a swarm of OpenAI agents is about architecture, not intentions. AI agents need protective layers—limited access, separate authorization for sensitive actions, records nobody can quietly edit, and outside testing before deployment—not a lecture about good behavior.

proj-syn.title: Are Mexicans Really Better Off Under Claudia Sheinbaum?
proj-syn.description: For two consecutive years, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has pointed to reductions in extreme poverty to argue that Mexicans are better off today than they were in 2018. But a more holistic look at the available socioeconomic data casts doubt on that rosy picture.

proj-syn.title: The UN’s Credibility Test
proj-syn.description: Effective multilateralism depends on institutions that are transparent, accountable, and able to enforce their own rules. The United Nations should lead by example, from how it selects its next secretary-general to how it plans to ensure that governments follow through on their climate commitments.

proj-syn.title: A Workable Social Contract for the Climate Transition
proj-syn.description: Economic insecurity and growing distrust in institutions are undermining governments’ ability to sustain support for climate action. To rebuild that support, they must show that climate policies can reduce household bills, create decent jobs, and ensure that the biggest emitters pay their fair share.

proj-syn.title: It’s Time to Reconsider Inflation Targeting
proj-syn.description: Central banks were caught off guard by the inflationary surge of 2021–23 because they relied too heavily on inflation forecasts based on flawed models and ignored other warning signs. Their failure to recognize the rapid growth of the money supply, in particular, underscores the need to reassess their reliance on inflation targeting.

proj-syn.title: Democrats Need to Talk About Immigration
proj-syn.description: Radical right-wing parties have advanced across Western countries by successfully tying immigration to voters’ diffuse fears about their economic well-being, personal security, and cultural identity. Rather than ignoring or co-opting such claims, mainstream parties must offer equally robust counternarratives.

proj-syn.title: War in an Age of Weak Powers
proj-syn.description: The war in Iran has weakened both the United States and China, exposing the limits of their military power and strategic influence. Their troubles are creating a more dangerous geopolitical landscape while providing Europe with a rare opportunity to reform its governance model and reinvent its global role.

proj-syn.title: Hedging the AI Doomsday Risk
proj-syn.description: As far-fetched as warnings of an impending AI apocalypse may sound, even a remote risk should not be dismissed outright when human extinction is at stake. To guard against a danger of such extraordinary scale, governments and companies need to go beyond conventional risk-management strategies.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Only as Trustworthy as the Internet
proj-syn.description: Trust in technology is eroding at the very moment AI is putting more power in the hands of governments and Big Tech. Rebuilding that trust requires keeping the internet open and accessible so that new technologies can develop through broad participation rather than being shaped by the interests of a powerful few.

proj-syn.title: AI Demands Simpler Financial Regulation
proj-syn.description: AI could undermine financial oversight by giving market participants new ways to circumvent rules that regulators never anticipated. Overly complicated regulations give AI agents more ways to game the system, underscoring the need to streamline existing frameworks and equip officials with AI tools of their own.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Asset Europe Has Overlooked
proj-syn.description: Europe’s soil is gradually dying, and yet the continent has still not recognized it as a strategic asset. Fortunately, the EU has many of the tools it needs to act, but doing so will require an overarching framework that helps farmers access financial rewards for measurable soil outcomes.

proj-syn.title: Why India Wants Peace in Ukraine—and China Doesn’t
proj-syn.description: The Ukraine war has turned Russia into a junior partner of China. This serves China's economic and strategic interests, but it creates major risks for India, which has long counted on Russia to help it counterbalance Chinese influence in the region.

proj-syn.title: AI and the Broken Career Ladder
proj-syn.description: AI can broaden access to expertise, support innovation, and boost economic growth. But shared prosperity will depend less on the performance of the next frontier model than on our ability to preserve skill formation, reorganize work, and distribute the gains equitably.

proj-syn.title: AI Firms’ Self-Serving Warnings
proj-syn.description: There is a method to the frontier AI labs’ marketing madness. They claim that AI will not only replace workers and expand the potential market from software budgets to labor-saving applications, but also that the existential risk associated with the technology justifies curtailing additional capital spending.

proj-syn.title: The UN Cannot—and Need Not—Wait for Consensus
proj-syn.description: Although the United Nations system remains the foundation of global governance, its capacity to drive domestic implementation of urgently needed reforms and regulations is stretched thin. Fortunately, narrower "plurilateral" arrangements can help, provided that they are explicitly designed to strengthen democracy.

proj-syn.title: The People Not Worth Replacing
proj-syn.description: At first glance, MAGA’s fear of immigrants and the rest of America’s fear of data centers have many similarities, with each reflecting insecurities about one’s place in a changing economy. But while the first fear tells natives that their place is valuable, the second assumes that it will soon be worth nothing.

proj-syn.title: What Amodei’s Call for an AI Pause Gets Wrong
proj-syn.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s recent appeal for a pause on AI development is a welcome one. But while AI companies do indeed need more breathing space to consider the full impact of their inventions before releasing them to the market, self-interested oversight is not the kind of governance we need.
